definition: The change in an object’s observed position due to motion of the object, the observer, or both.
intuition: A rotating observer sees distant stationary objects shift across their field of view. Earth’s eastward rotation makes the sky appear to turn westward.
misconceptions: Daily apparent motion does not imply stars orbit Earth each day.
takeaway: Where something appears depends on the observer’s motion.

source.section: Looking Out from a Spinning, Round Earth
